claims.text: Human review is mandatory here and the AI may not rule at all. The dispute is flagged safety-related, and the record itself carries the safety indicator: at 22:20:30, two minutes before he cancelled, the driver wrote 'U think I free ah? Come down now or I come up find you' — a threat to come up to the rider — and the rider answered at 22:21:00 'Why are you talking to me like that? I'm scared to come down now.' POL-GEN-21 applies 'whatever the category the filer chose': the AI may gather evidence and prepare the case file, but it may not issue a ruling, determine fault or recommend a resolution on a record carrying a threat of this kind. The only lawful disposition is ESCALATE, which holds the 5.00 SGD rather than collecting it.

The driver's answer that he 'was joking only' does not undo the threat. The message is a plain threat to come up to the rider's location, it was delivered at 22:20:31 and read at 22:20:51, the rider answered in fear within thirty seconds, and the driver cancelled and applied the fee two minutes later. A threat is judged by what it says and by how it was received, not by the sender's later characterisation; POL-GEN-21 lists a threat of assault and a rider feeling unsafe as safety indicators, and both are on this record. Nothing in the driver's statement supplies any other explanation for why the rider did not board.

The no-show clause's finality does not survive the safety gateway. POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final 'subject to POL-GEN-21 (safety)' — the safety exception is written into the finality rule itself. The value band does not save it either: the contested amount is 5.00 SGD, which is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, but POL-GEN-22 supplies only the confidence a ruling needs; it cannot license a ruling that POL-GEN-21 forbids. Where the gateway opens, the case goes to a human reviewer and the fee is held.

If the judge reaches the money at all, POL-NS-23 voids the fee in full. That clause requires the driver to have messaged and called the rider before cancelling, and says that if either limb is missing the fee is voided: FULL_REFUND of the fee charged, with no driver compensation. The derived contact_before_cancel flag reports obligation_met as true on a message-count reading, and I do not hide that; the rider's position is a construction point. The second of the two pre-cancellation messages is the threat itself, and a message whose content is 'come down now or I come up find you' is an act of intimidation, not the contact the clause exists to secure — it is the very message that drove the rider away from the car. On the rider's reading the contact obligation is not discharged, and 5.00 SGD is due back to her in full.

The 5.00 SGD charge is not a rider no-show fee on this record. The fee POL-NS-22 authorises stands only where the driver waited his free wait and the rider then failed to board; the free wait on this on-demand trip ran from the driver's arrival at 22:16:30 to 22:21:30 (POL-NS-21), and inside that window the rider had already told the driver at 22:19:10 that she was 'Coming, 2 min'. The only thing that then changed was the driver's 22:20:30 message. The rider did not decline to show; she was kept away from the car by the driver's own conduct, and the disputed charge should not be left on her payment method.

Escalation is the disposition that protects the rider's money while the case is reviewed. POL-GEN-03 says ESCALATE is always terminal, replaces any ruling, issues no monetary outcome, and leaves the amount held. The payments ledger shows the 5.00 SGD already charged with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the present state is that the rider is carrying the disputed charge; a ruling that escalates, rather than one that lets the fee stand, is what stops her carrying a charge incurred after the driver threatened her.

One fact the no-show timetable needs cannot be fixed on this record, which is a further reason to escalate rather than rule. This is an on-demand trip with scheduled_at null, so the deadline POL-NS-24 fixes — the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes — cannot be computed at all; POL-NS-24's own note directs that where the record carries no scheduled time and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies. POL-GEN-26 requires escalation with the open question stated, and forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence. The open question is what, if anything, beyond the driver's threat justified treating this rider as a no-show.

claims.text: The driver arrived at 22:16:30 and cancelled at 22:22:50 - 380 seconds later - so the 300-second free wait POL-NS-21 fixes for an on-demand trip had fully run before the cancellation. The GPS trace corroborates the arrival: its nearest fix lies 1.0 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 4.0 m, far inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. The no-show was validly declared.

Both limbs of POL-NS-23's contact obligation are met before the 22:22:50 cancellation: the driver sent in-app chat messages at 22:16:50 and 22:20:30, and placed an in-app call at 22:18:00 (unanswered, 15 s), all carried in the trip record and the chat log. Nothing in POL-NS-23 voids the fee, and the rider has identified no other clause that would.

The rider's own chat message at 22:19:10 - 'Coming, 2 min' - shows she was aware of the driver and still had not boarded the car when the free wait expired at 22:21:30 and the driver cancelled at 22:22:50. The no-show is established on the rider's own words, not merely on the driver's timer.

The payments ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line of exactly 5.00 SGD, matching the policy no-show fee, so POL-NS-22 entitles the driver to that sum as compensation for time and fuel, and the amount-mismatch referral provided by that clause is not triggered.

The one no-show clause that favours the rider, POL-NS-24, does not apply: this is an on-demand trip with no scheduled pickup time, so the driver-late deadline cannot be fixed, and the driver's arrival at 22:16:30 is on the record. The rider's statement that she was afraid to come down supplies no clause-based ground for returning the fee to her.

The dispute is flagged safety-related and the chat log records the rider saying she was scared after the driver's message, so POL-GEN-21 sends the whole case to human review whatever the category and forbids the AI from issuing a ruling, determining fault or recommending a resolution of its own. On escalation the 5.00 SGD fee is held rather than returned under POL-GEN-03. The rider's demand for a refund therefore cannot issue from the AI, and the driver's charge stands pending review.
